legend: Given a positive integer sequence a1,a2,⋯,an%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%%, you need to perform exactly k%%ZSMJ2%% operations. For each operation, you need to choose one element and increase its value by 1%%ZSMJ3%%.
Maximize the greatest common divisor of all elements after the operations.
input: There are multiple test cases. The first line of the input contains an integer T%%ZSMJ4%% (1≤T≤103%%ZSMJ5%%), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:
The first line contains two integers n%%ZSMJ6%% and k%%ZSMJ7%% (1≤n≤106%%ZSMJ8%%, 1≤k≤1012%%ZSMJ9%%) indicating the length of the sequence and the number of operations.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ10%% integers a1,a2,⋯,an%%ZSMJ11%% (1≤ai≤106%%ZSMJ12%%) indicating the sequence.

It's guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ13%% of all test cases will not exceed 106%%ZSMJ14%%, the sum of maxai%%ZSMJ15%% of all test cases will not exceed 106%%ZSMJ16%%, and the sum of k%%ZSMJ17%% of all test cases will not exceed 1012%%ZSMJ18%%.
output: For each test case output one line containing one integer, indicating the maximum possible greatest common divisor of all elements after exactly k%%ZSMJ19%% operations.
note: For the first sample test case, we can change the sequence to 5,10,10%%ZSMJ20%%, and the greatest common divisor is 5%%ZSMJ21%%.
For the second sample test case, we can change the sequence to 6,10,10%%ZSMJ22%%, and the greatest common divisor is 2%%ZSMJ23%%.
